corrkit: correlation analyses with annotated heatmaps and tables

Source: R/corrkit-package.R
corrkit-package.Rd

corrkit does not compute correlations itself: it calls validated engines and adds a way of working on top of them.

Details

Engines (an existing function for every computation, with a base-R fallback when a suggested package is missing)

  • one pair, unadjusted: stats::cor.test()

  • one pair, partial: ppcor::pcor.test() (Kim 2015, doi:10.5351/CSAM.2015.22.6.665)

  • matrix of all pairs: psych::corr.test() or correlation::correlation() (Makowski et al. 2020, doi:10.21105/joss.02306), always with raw p-values; the adjustment is done by corrkit with stats::p.adjust() over an explicit family

  • binary effect sizes: stats::t.test(), stats::wilcox.test(), effectsize::rank_biserial() for the confidence interval

What corrkit adds

  • an explicit multiple-testing family (adjust_by, BH by default);

  • a dedicated treatment of binary (0/1) variables: separate blocks in the plots, a [0/1] marker, a reading note (cor_binary_note()) and the effect sizes to report instead of the correlation (cor_binary_effects());

  • outputs whose subtitle, caption or source notes state the method, the engine, the formulas, the adjustment and how to read them: plot_cor_heatmap(), plot_cor_cross(), plot_cor_pair(), tbl_cor_matrix(), tbl_cor_cross(), tbl_cor_long(), tbl_cor_binary().

Start with vignette("corrkit").
